python_functions.name: choose_correction
python_functions.signature: choose_correction(state, stage: str, evidence: dict, options: list[dict], default_id: str)
python_functions.purpose: Asks the optional GPT advisor to select only one supplied candidate ID, validates its structured response, and returns the corresponding existing candidate. It caps model calls, records an audit event, and falls back to the deterministic default on refusal, invalid output or service failure.

python_functions.name: run_a1_requirements
python_functions.purpose: Validates the input grid, resolves declared load combinations, initializes active profiles and records the workflow/reference basis. Invalid input becomes an A1 failure before model modification.

python_functions.name: run_a2_readiness
python_functions.purpose: Checks live enablement, a saved idle analytical STAAD model, IDEA service/SDK product-release compatibility, a saved Tekla model and template availability. It records actual readiness instead of assuming that an open window means an API is ready.

python_functions.name: _lookup_profile_param
python_functions.purpose: Safely probes a profile-parameter getter for geometry generation, returning zero when the lookup fails.

python_functions.name: _fallback_dimension
python_functions.purpose: Provides legacy dimension lookup/parsing for generation helpers. The live A3 path separately validates installed catalogue dimensions before generation, so a fallback alone does not establish live readiness.

python_functions.name: _lookup_profile_height
python_functions.purpose: Looks up Tekla height and retains the legacy generation-only fallback if lookup is unavailable. Live catalogue validation remains a separate prerequisite.

python_functions.name: _lookup_profile_width
python_functions.purpose: Looks up Tekla width with the legacy generation helper fallback; it is not a substitute for live catalogue verification.

python_functions.name: generate_members
python_functions.purpose: Generates physical CAD members, split analytical members and a summary from the same grid. It accounts for section dimensions, offsets and mirrored bracing while preserving cross-tool names.

python_functions.name: generate_members.point
python_functions.signature: point(i: int, j: int, z: float)
python_functions.purpose: Nested generator helper that produces a grid-space physical point from bay indices and elevation.

python_functions.name: generate_members.transform_to_staad_co_ordinates
python_functions.purpose: Converts a generated physical point to the analytical STAAD coordinate convention, maintaining the explicit difference between CAD and analysis axes.

python_functions.name: check_geometry
python_functions.purpose: Rejects missing, invalid, nonfinite, zero-length, duplicate or disconnected analytical geometry before sending it to the desktop solver.

python_functions.name: run_a3_frame_generator
python_functions.purpose: Applies active correction profiles to the grid, validates catalogues and geometry, generates the frame and declares its connection plan. It increments design generation and rejects missing templates required by that plan.

python_functions.name: validate_profile_catalogue
python_functions.purpose: Requires positive dimensions from the actual installed Tekla catalogue for all selected profiles before a live frame is generated.

python_functions.name: send_to_staad
python_functions.purpose: A4's thin adapter delegates to the live implementation; the radiator implementation resets/builds STAAD, assigns verified properties/loads, runs unattended analysis and extracts forces, design ratios and normalized displacements. Live errors are not replaced by simulation.

python_functions.name: grade_staad_results
python_functions.purpose: First rejects invalid/incomplete live evidence, then checks all returned member-type ratios and serviceability drift. It returns a boolean grade plus an allowed correction target only for a supported engineering failure.

python_functions.name: run_a4_staad_analyzer
python_functions.purpose: Clears downstream evidence, analyzes the current frame and grades it. A permitted failed frame selects a larger catalogue candidate, records an actual profile change and routes through A3 again; unrecoverable or invalid evidence stops.

python_functions.name: _to_jsonable
python_functions.purpose: Converts SDK enums/models and nested objects to ordinary JSON-compatible data for exported evidence and API handling.

python_functions.name: _get_client
python_functions.purpose: Attaches to the already-running IDEA Connection REST API service. It does not silently start a substitute offline solver.

python_functions.name: _resolve_connection
python_functions.purpose: Selects the intended connection by ID, index or unique name. Missing and ambiguous matches are errors.

python_functions.name: _resolve_member
python_functions.purpose: Resolves an exact or unique member-name match and rejects ambiguous/missing members instead of dropping their loads or properties.

python_functions.name: _section_update_member
python_functions.purpose: Handles the senior transverse-placeholder name explicitly when the template contains only the actual aligned transverse beam. Subsequent verification permits a no-op only when its section/material already match.

python_functions.name: _free_end_position
python_functions.purpose: Infers a member's free end from connected_by when an effect does not specify a position. Missing connection-end information fails rather than guessing.

python_functions.name: _resolve_cross_section_id
python_functions.signature: _resolve_cross_section_id(api_client, project_id: str, mprl_cross_section_name: str, mprl_material_name: str)
python_functions.purpose: Reuses or adds a section only when both section name and embedded material name match the requested catalogue identity. Added material/section evidence is checked before its ID is accepted.

python_functions.name: _resolve_cross_section_id.matching
python_functions.purpose: Nested section/material matcher that normalizes whitespace/case and examines the material embedded in each IDEA cross-section record.

python_functions.name: _list_operations
python_functions.purpose: Returns the selected connection's IDEA operations for diagnostics and supported parameter inspection.

python_functions.name: _list_operations_properties
python_functions.purpose: Returns common operation properties from the SDK for connection inspection.

python_functions.name: _get_parameters
python_functions.signature: _get_parameters(api_client, project_id: str, connection_id: int, include_hidden: bool=False)
python_functions.purpose: Reads exposed IDEA parameters, optionally including hidden fields for diagnostics. Corrections may only update supported exposed keys.

python_functions.name: _find_parameters
python_functions.signature: _find_parameters(api_client, project_id: str, connection_id: int, name_contains: str, include_hidden: bool=True)
python_functions.purpose: Filters IDEA parameters by key/description text for diagnostic discovery.

python_functions.name: _quote_expression_if_needed
python_functions.purpose: Leaves numeric or already quoted expressions intact and quotes textual expressions for IDEA's expression interface.

python_functions.name: _set_parameters
python_functions.signature: _set_parameters(api_client, project_id: str, connection_id: int, updates: List[Dict[str, str]])
python_functions.purpose: Sends typed SDK parameter-update objects and propagates failures, rather than recording a proposed correction as though it had been applied.

python_functions.name: to_json_convention_string
python_functions.purpose: Formats SDK-derived data as JSON for inspection through the shared converter.

python_functions.name: _validate_template_limits
python_functions.purpose: Checks the template's enabled local-deformation check and physical plastic-strain/deformation limits before summary utilization is graded.

python_functions.name: design_joint
python_functions.purpose: Opens the exact template; checks topology, sections/materials and brace angles; replaces template loads with actual effects; applies/reads back parameters; validates physical settings; calculates and exports a saved project and checks. Every integration failure remains visible.

python_functions.name: design_joint.progress
python_functions.purpose: Nested adapter callback that prints the current IDEA/Tekla phase and reports it to the worker when supplied. It reports activity, not engineering acceptance.

python_functions.name: grade_joint_check_summary
python_functions.purpose: Interprets IDEA check_value as utilization percent, checks finite values and SDK statuses, and identifies a permitted size category for a numeric exceedance. A false SDK status within the numeric limit is unresolved evidence, not permission for a blind retry.

python_functions.name: _connection_payload
python_functions.purpose: Builds one scoped IDEA request from all strength envelopes, explicit template aliases and the declared reference material mapping. It refuses global-force input, empty loads, inconsistent properties and missing templates.

python_functions.name: _connection_signature
python_functions.purpose: Hashes the complete calculational payload, design generation and template content so only unchanged passing connection evidence can be reused.
calls: hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({'generation': generation, 'payload': payload, 'template_hash': template_hash}, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False).encode()).hexdigest
json.dumps({'generation': generation, 'payload': payload, 'template_hash': template_hash}, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False).encode

python_functions.name: _correct_connection_parameters
python_functions.purpose: Steps only exposed numeric parameters that match the failing size category and returns both proposed overrides and an explicit old/new change list.

python_functions.name: run_a5_ideastatica_analyzer
python_functions.purpose: Calculates required IDEA families, reuses only matching passing evidence, grades actual checks and runs bounded per-family detailing corrections. No-op changes, repeated unchanged checks, unsupported parameters and exhausted retries stop the run.

python_functions.name: run_a5_ideastatica_analyzer.update_progress
python_functions.purpose: Nested A5/A7 callback that saves phase/status messages for UI polling and the watchdog. A5 declares a bounded multi-effect calculation budget when it starts FEA.

python_functions.name: run_a6_package_validator
python_functions.purpose: Independently regrades source evidence, checks frame/connection signatures and scope, then builds the evaluated Tekla handoff and package hash. Failed evidence triggers bounded recovery or terminal failure; cached PASS flags alone are insufficient.

python_functions.name: _index_to_letters
python_functions.purpose: Converts a positive grid index to spreadsheet-style labels, including rollover beyond Z.

python_functions.name: generate_y_axis_labels
python_functions.purpose: Creates the transverse grid-label sequence for the configured number of bays.

python_functions.name: get_bolt_parameters
python_functions.purpose: Returns the existing bolt-hole tolerance, hole diameter and edge-distance rule for the selected diameter. It supports reference detailing geometry; it does not replace IDEA bolt checks.

python_functions.name: _catalog_dimension
python_functions.purpose: Requires a finite positive installed Tekla dimension for the modeler's connection-geometry calculations.

python_functions.name: get_profile_width
python_functions.purpose: Returns the profile width from the installed Tekla catalogue; A7 validates that it is finite and positive.

python_functions.name: get_profile_height
python_functions.purpose: Returns the profile height from the installed Tekla catalogue. A7's wrapper requires a finite positive result rather than guessing.

python_functions.name: get_profile_web_thickness
python_functions.purpose: Reads the profile web/wall thickness used by the reference connection-geometry calculations.

python_functions.name: clean_tekla
python_functions.purpose: Enumerates the active model, preserves grids/grid surfaces and DefaultGroup, removes components before remaining parts, verifies cleanup and saves. Optional callbacks report long scans/deletions; failures propagate.

python_functions.name: modify_grid
python_functions.signature: modify_grid(model, coord_x, coord_y, coord_z, label_x, label_y, label_z)
python_functions.purpose: Updates existing grid coordinates/labels or delegates to the shared grid helper. A7 derives levels from the actual generated geometry instead of fixed sample heights.

python_functions.name: connection_attributes
python_functions.signature: connection_attributes(joint_groups: dict, joint_group_ids, connection_number: int, bracing: Optional[str]=None)
python_functions.purpose: Maps evaluated IDEA parameter keys to component attributes and converts metres to millimetres. It handles the double-brace transverse D2 namespace and rejects invalid numeric mapped values.

python_functions.name: joint_group_columns
python_functions.purpose: Builds the column-name set for each calculated family so connection parameters reach the relevant physical columns.

python_functions.name: joint_group_beam_pairs
python_functions.purpose: Builds longitudinal/transverse physical beam pairs at the family joints for component-30 parameter assignment.

python_functions.name: _component_integer
python_functions.purpose: Creates an explicit .NET Int32 for integer component attributes. This avoids pythonnet choosing the ref-double overload during read-back.

python_functions.name: set_component_attribute
python_functions.purpose: Selects integer, string or floating-point SetAttribute handling according to the component field. Explicit rejection propagates to the publication result.

python_functions.name: _verify_component
python_functions.purpose: Selects the inserted component again and checks requested attributes using the proper typed GetAttribute overload and numeric/string comparisons.

python_functions.name: add_base_connection
python_functions.signature: add_base_connection(model, column, connection_number: int, detail_name: str, design_code: str, grid_specs: dict, attribute_file: str='baseplate_1004', attributes: Optional[dict]=None)
python_functions.purpose: Loads the existing 1004 attribute preset, applies requested overrides, assigns the column/reference point and inserts the detail. It verifies the inserted component rather than assuming Insert or loading succeeded.

python_functions.name: add_column2beam_connection
python_functions.signature: add_column2beam_connection(model, secondary, primary, connection_number: int, detail_name: str, design_code: str, grid_specs: dict, classCode: int, attribute_file: str='column_longitudinal_beam', upVector=None, attributes: Optional[dict]=None)
python_functions.purpose: Loads the chosen standard component preset, assigns primary/secondary members, applies attributes and positioning, inserts it and verifies its persisted attributes.

python_functions.name: _stringify
python_functions.purpose: Safely turns diagnostic property values into displayable strings.

python_functions.name: dump_attributes
python_functions.purpose: Collects .NET object properties and user properties for diagnostic inspection, reporting read errors as diagnostics.

python_functions.name: print_attributes
python_functions.purpose: Prints a structured object's diagnostic attributes; it is not an acceptance checker.

python_functions.name: pick_and_print_attributes
python_functions.purpose: Interactive diagnostic utility for objects selected in Tekla. The automatic graph does not require this manual picker.

python_functions.name: send_to_tekla
python_functions.purpose: Resets the target model, supplies missing reference assets, sets the actual grid, inserts physical members and standard/calculated component attributes, verifies geometry/profile/materials and saves on success. It returns counts and concrete errors; it cannot return a simulated live pass.

python_functions.name: send_to_tekla.progress
python_functions.purpose: Nested adapter callback that prints the current IDEA/Tekla phase and reports it to the worker when supplied. It reports activity, not engineering acceptance.

python_functions.name: send_to_tekla.connect
python_functions.purpose: Nested modeler wrapper that records each successfully inserted/verified component ID and reports progress in batches.

python_functions.name: run_a7_tekla_modeler
python_functions.purpose: Requires a passing A6 package, sends only its validated handoff to Tekla and checks member counts, verification counts, simulation flags and errors. Incomplete publication is terminal and described concisely while full diagnostics remain in state.

python_functions.name: run_a7_tekla_modeler.update_progress
python_functions.purpose: Nested A5/A7 callback that saves phase/status messages for UI polling and the watchdog. A5 declares a bounded multi-effect calculation budget when it starts FEA.

python_functions.name: run_a8_reporting
python_functions.purpose: Builds the calculation summary, scope, correction history, connection results and source-run lineage. It ends automation at PAUSED_AT_GATE3, awaiting the responsible engineer's acceptance.

python_functions.name: accept_gate3
python_functions.signature: accept_gate3(state: WorkflowState, engineer_name: str='Lead Structural Engineer')
python_functions.purpose: Requires a validated package already awaiting review with A7 PASSED, then records the named engineer and timestamp and marks COMPLETED. It cannot approve an arbitrary failed run.

python_functions.name: section_exists
python_functions.signature: section_exists(profile: str, country: str='EUROPE', directory: Path | None=None)
python_functions.purpose: Reads the installed European STAAD section databases in read-only mode and checks the translated section name. Unsupported countries or unavailable catalogue entries return False; a guessed section is not accepted.

python_functions.name: frame_options
python_functions.signature: frame_options(current: str, target: str, country: str='EUROPE')
python_functions.purpose: Filters the larger entries in the configured column, beam or brace ladder against STAAD availability and positive Tekla dimensions. It returns named candidates for the correction selector; availability is not an independent engineering approval.

python_functions.name: preview_joint_groups
python_functions.purpose: Builds a temporary node/member connectivity dictionary from generated analytical members, then uses the same grouping logic as STAAD. It plans connection families without calling model-changing OpenSTAAD methods.

python_functions.name: template_coverage
python_functions.purpose: Compares previewed joint-family names with available IDEA filenames and returns required, available and missing families plus the preview. Reference-scope planning subsequently distinguishes calculated families from standard details.

python_functions.name: workflow_mode
python_functions.purpose: Reads and validates the workflow mode. Only poc1_automation, poc2_automation and reviewed_engineering are accepted.

python_functions.name: load_environment
python_functions.purpose: Reads simple KEY=value settings from the repository .env without evaluating shell commands or interpolation. Existing process environment values win; credentials are not copied into workflow state.

python_functions.name: _integer
python_functions.purpose: Parses an integer setting and enforces a minimum. Invalid revision, timeout or call-limit values fail configuration rather than silently becoming usable defaults.

python_functions.name: settings
python_functions.purpose: Returns an immutable Settings instance containing the configuration actually consumed by this application. A setting present in .env is not necessarily implemented unless code reads it.

python_functions.name: frame_signature
python_functions.purpose: Serializes the current grid, loads, physical members and analytical members in a stable order and computes SHA-256. A6 compares this signature with the one attached to the STAAD result.

python_functions.name: RunController.__init__
python_functions.purpose: Initializes the active run ID, owned worker handle and cancellation flag. One controller instance tracks one worker at a time.

python_functions.name: RunController._terminate
python_functions.purpose: Stops only the owned worker process tree and awaits its exit. On Windows it invokes taskkill for that worker; an external IDEA REST service is not necessarily part of this tree.

python_functions.name: RunController.cancel
python_functions.purpose: Checks that the requested run belongs to this controller, marks cancellation and terminates its worker. Cancellation during process startup is also handled.

python_functions.name: RunController.execute
python_functions.signature: execute(self, payload: dict, run_id: str, resume_state: WorkflowState | None=None)
python_functions.purpose: Persists initial input, starts the disposable STA worker, captures its log, polls durable progress and enforces time budgets. It records worker crashes, cancellations and timeouts as terminal outcomes, and supports a prepared publication-only retry.

python_functions.name: get_next_profile
python_functions.purpose: Returns the next configured profile for a recognized member category. Unknown profiles and ladder ceilings do not justify inventing a new section.

python_functions.name: get_next_plate_thickness
python_functions.purpose: Returns the next configured plate thickness in millimetres, or the ceiling. The caller must check that a real increase occurred.

python_functions.name: get_next_bolt_diameter
python_functions.purpose: Returns the next configured bolt diameter in millimetres. It changes only a proposed parameter; IDEA must still rerun and pass.

python_functions.name: get_next_weld_size
python_functions.purpose: Returns the next configured weld size in millimetres. This is a bounded candidate generator, not a weld-capacity calculation.

python_functions.name: step_parameter_expression
python_functions.signature: step_parameter_expression(key: str, expression: str, fix_type: str='auto')
python_functions.purpose: Steps a finite positive numeric expression through the appropriate sizing ladder while preserving its metre/mm convention. Formula strings, invalid values and ceiling values are not arbitrarily rewritten.

python_functions.name: reference_combinations
python_functions.purpose: Creates the senior procedure's exact eight combinations and three envelope IDs. The original opposing-direction factors are preserved only as the declared reference procedure, not relabeled as independently approved project criteria.

python_functions.name: validate_combinations
python_functions.purpose: Checks required keys, unique names, known load cases, finite nonzero factors and both serviceability/strength coverage. Custom combinations reject opposing wind and temperature cases; the exact declared reference set has an explicit compatibility exception.

python_functions.name: resolve_combinations
python_functions.purpose: Resolves combinations from the run payload, then the configured JSON file, then automation-mode reference defaults. Reviewed mode requires explicit input; the resolved combinations are validated before model changes.

python_functions.name: _sync_state
python_functions.purpose: Saves graph progress to the durable store and updates the server cache when available. Its wrapper catches synchronization exceptions; persistence is not a distributed transaction with the external engineering applications.

python_functions.name: _start_agent
python_functions.purpose: Sets the current agent and RUNNING message, then synchronizes progress before a node begins its work.

python_functions.name: node_a1
python_functions.purpose: LangGraph wrapper for A1: records RUNNING, calls the stage implementation and persists the returned state. It separates stage logic from graph orchestration.

python_functions.name: node_a2
python_functions.purpose: LangGraph wrapper for A2: records RUNNING, calls the stage implementation and persists the returned state. It separates stage logic from graph orchestration.

python_functions.name: node_a3
python_functions.purpose: LangGraph wrapper for A3: records RUNNING, calls the stage implementation and persists the returned state. It separates stage logic from graph orchestration.

python_functions.name: node_a4
python_functions.purpose: LangGraph wrapper for A4: records RUNNING, calls the stage implementation and persists the returned state. It separates stage logic from graph orchestration.

python_functions.name: node_a5
python_functions.purpose: LangGraph wrapper for A5: records RUNNING, calls the stage implementation and persists the returned state. It separates stage logic from graph orchestration.

python_functions.name: node_a6
python_functions.purpose: LangGraph wrapper for A6: records RUNNING, calls the stage implementation and persists the returned state. It separates stage logic from graph orchestration.

python_functions.name: node_a7
python_functions.purpose: LangGraph wrapper for A7: records RUNNING, calls the stage implementation and persists the returned state. It separates stage logic from graph orchestration.

python_functions.name: node_a8
python_functions.purpose: LangGraph wrapper for A8: records RUNNING, calls the stage implementation and persists the returned state. It separates stage logic from graph orchestration.

python_functions.name: route_after_a4
python_functions.purpose: Ends on failure, returns to A3 for a permitted frame revision, or advances a passing frame to A5. Routing uses explicit stage status rather than trusting a progress label.

python_functions.name: route_after_a5
python_functions.purpose: Ends on terminal connection failure, reruns A5 after an actual parameter revision, or advances a passing scoped connection package to A6.

python_functions.name: route_after_a6
python_functions.purpose: Routes a bounded validation recovery to A3 or A5, advances a valid package to A7, or ends a failed audit.

python_functions.name: build_workflow_graph
python_functions.purpose: Registers the eight LangGraph nodes, sequential edges and conditional correction/recovery edges. Failed early stages terminate; the workflow does not continue merely to color every stage green.

python_functions.name: run_agentic_workflow
python_functions.purpose: Creates typed initial state with configured limits, compiles the graph and invokes it with a bounded recursion setting. On graph exceptions it records failure against the latest saved stage.

python_functions.name: prepare_publication_retry
python_functions.purpose: Requires a failed A7 run with a validated calculation package, deep-copies it into a new run, records lineage and clears old publication/acceptance data. It cannot be used to skip a failed A4 or A5.

python_functions.name: run_publication_retry
python_functions.purpose: Runs A6 again against retained source evidence, stops if evidence changed or failed, and only then reruns A7 and A8. It avoids repeating unchanged FEA solely to repair a Tekla handoff.

python_functions.name: build_connection_scope
python_functions.purpose: Constructs the explicit split between required IDEA families and standard-detail families. Automation follows the senior procedure; reviewed mode requires all families. It records component presets and the reference material-catalogue mapping.

python_functions.name: scope_for_state
python_functions.purpose: Audits exact, nonoverlapping family coverage and rejects stale plans, dropped required inner calculations or altered reference presets/material mappings. A legacy state with no declared plan retains full coverage.

python_functions.name: template_for_group
python_functions.purpose: Resolves an exact filename or the explicit inner double-brace alias in reference mode. It does not choose an unrelated template by similarity.

python_functions.name: start_agentic_run
python_functions.purpose: Acquires the API's run lock, assigns a new run ID and waits for the managed worker's final state. Concurrent runs through this server receive HTTP 409.

python_functions.name: get_active_run
python_functions.purpose: Returns the durable snapshot of the controller's current run, or null when idle. Browser progress polling uses this read-only endpoint.

python_functions.name: retry_publication
python_functions.purpose: Looks up a failed source run, prepares an eligible publication retry and executes it under the same tool lock. It preserves the failed source and returns the new tracked run.

python_functions.name: cancel_run
python_functions.purpose: Delegates a stop request to the controller and rejects requests for runs it does not own. The eventual durable state records the cancellation outcome.

python_functions.name: list_recent_runs
python_functions.purpose: Returns recent durable run metadata for history and page-refresh restoration.

python_functions.name: get_run_status
python_functions.purpose: Loads one saved run and serializes it for the browser. Missing run IDs return HTTP 404; integer result keys survive JSON conversion.

python_functions.name: accept_run
python_functions.purpose: Loads a package, invokes the final acceptance guard, persists its accepted state and returns it. It does not make failed or cancelled runs acceptable.

python_functions.name: fail_workflow
python_functions.signature: fail_workflow(state: WorkflowState, agent_id: str, message: str)
python_functions.purpose: Sets FAILED, the current agent and an explanatory error, updates the stage status and appends a timestamped log. It keeps ended failures from appearing to run forever.

python_functions.name: monotonic_now_iso
python_functions.purpose: Produces strictly increasing UTC timestamps for saved run ordering, including rapid writes in the same process. This is a storage-order helper, not an engineering clock.

python_functions.name: SqliteWorkflowStore.__init__
python_functions.purpose: Creates the database directory, synchronization lock/cache and required SQLite tables/indexes.

python_functions.name: SqliteWorkflowStore._connection
python_functions.purpose: Provides a context-managed SQLite connection with named rows and a lock-wait timeout, closing it afterward.

python_functions.name: SqliteWorkflowStore._init_db
python_functions.purpose: Creates workflow_runs, workflow_events and the status index if absent. This implementation uses local SQLite, not a PostgreSQL migration framework.

python_functions.name: SqliteWorkflowStore.save_state
python_functions.purpose: Upserts a complete serialized state snapshot and commits it atomically in SQLite. It preserves the original created_at on updates and advances updated_at.

python_functions.name: SqliteWorkflowStore.get_state
python_functions.purpose: Reads state from SQLite on every call so another process's changes are visible. It then refreshes the in-process cache and validates the stored model.
calls: conn.execute('SELECT state_json FROM workflow_runs WHERE run_id = ?', (run_id,)).fetchone

python_functions.name: SqliteWorkflowStore.list_runs
python_functions.purpose: Returns run metadata ordered by most recent update, bounded by the requested limit.
calls:
conn.execute('
                    SELECT run_id, status, current_agent, created_at, updated_at
                    FROM workflow_runs
                    ORDER BY updated_at DESC
                    LIMIT ?
                ', (limit,)).fetchall

python_functions.name: SqliteWorkflowStore.record_log
python_functions.purpose: Inserts a structured event row and commits it. Snapshot logs and event rows should not be confused with a LangGraph checkpointer.

python_functions.name: main
python_functions.purpose: Loads a saved run, initializes a Windows STA COM apartment before pythonnet imports, executes the full graph or publication-only recovery, and persists the terminal result.

python_functions.name: load_json
python_functions.purpose: Reads a UTF-8 JSON file for the command-line handoff builder and returns its decoded data.

python_functions.name: load_operation_parameters
python_functions.purpose: Accepts a parameter list or an object containing operation_parameters and checks each entry has key and expression.

python_functions.name: build_design_input
python_functions.signature: build_design_input(staad_output: Dict[str, Any], operation_parameters: List[Dict[str, Any]], envelope_id: str, joint_group_id: str)
python_functions.purpose: Builds the senior-style manual IDEA payload for one explicit envelope and family, using actual STAAD loads and properties. It rejects missing families and empty effects.

python_functions.name: main
python_functions.purpose: Parses CLI arguments, loads STAAD/parameter JSON, builds one manual IDEA input and writes it to disk.

python_functions.name: load_json
python_functions.purpose: Reads a UTF-8 JSON file for the command-line handoff builder and returns its decoded data.

python_functions.name: _warn
python_functions.purpose: Writes a command-line handoff-builder diagnostic to stderr. These legacy warnings are not the automated A6 acceptance policy.

python_functions.name: build_joint_groups
python_functions.signature: build_joint_groups(staad_output: Dict[str, Any], idea_outputs: List[Dict[str, Any]], idea_output_paths: List[str])

python_functions.name: main
python_functions.purpose: Parses CLI arguments, loads generated geometry plus selected IDEA outputs and writes the manual Tekla handoff JSON.

python_functions.name: searchDictByKeyStart
python_functions.purpose: Returns the value of the first dictionary entry whose key starts with the requested prefix, or None if no entry matches. It does not return a filtered dictionary.

python_functions.name: get_ubc97_ce
python_functions.purpose: Interpolates the existing UBC97 exposure coefficient table by height, with explicit low/high-height handling and invalid-exposure rejection. Its table is a project/reference input, not a newly derived standard.

python_functions.name: calculate_wind_pressure_profile
python_functions.signature: calculate_wind_pressure_profile(wind_speed_mph: float, wind_exposure_category: str, frame_pressure_coefficient_cq: float, iw: float=1.0)
python_functions.purpose: Calculates the reference pressure profile from exposure, speed, frame coefficient and importance factor, returning heights and pressures. The PDF explains the implementation rather than independently certifying the load model.

python_functions.name: tekla2staad
python_functions.purpose: Normalizes profile/material strings and translates them to STAAD conventions. The assignment path separately handles European cold-formed tables and verifies actual section/material read-back.

python_functions.name: tekla2ideastatica_profile

python_functions.name: country2code
python_functions.purpose: Maps a country label to the configured STAAD section-table code, returning an invalid sentinel for an unknown label.

python_functions.name: _SequentialIdAllocator.__init__
python_functions.purpose: Initializes a deterministic noncolliding node/member ID sequence for newly generated STAAD entities.

python_functions.name: _SequentialIdAllocator.next
python_functions.purpose: Returns the current entity ID and advances the sequence.

python_functions.name: _get_openstaad
python_functions.purpose: Connects to the running OpenSTAAD analytical session and enables silent mode. Connection problems propagate as an adapter error.

python_functions.name: _format_com_error
python_functions.purpose: Formats COM exceptions into an actionable diagnostic without pretending a failed call succeeded.

python_functions.name: _node_key
python_functions.purpose: Rounds coordinates into a consistent node-cache key so coincident beam endpoints can share one analytical node.

python_functions.name: _get_or_create_node

python_functions.name: _create_beam
python_functions.signature: _create_beam(geometry: OSGeometry, node_cache: Dict[tuple, int], node_ids: '_SequentialIdAllocator', beam_ids: '_SequentialIdAllocator', member: dict)
python_functions.purpose: Creates one member in the relevant live application. In STAAD it resolves shared nodes and creates the analytical beam; in Tekla it sets physical endpoints, profile, material, class and positioning before insertion.

python_functions.name: _resolve_profile_name
python_functions.purpose: Looks up the configured STAAD profile-name translation instead of synthesizing an arbitrary replacement.

python_functions.name: _assign_property
python_functions.signature: _assign_property(property: OSProperty, beam_no: int, member: dict, property_id_cache: Optional[Dict[str, int]]=None, country: str='EUROPE')
python_functions.purpose: Creates/reuses a STAAD section property in the proper table, assigns it and its material, and reads both identities back. An SDK boolean alone is not accepted as evidence of assignment.

python_functions.name: _create_combo_load_case
python_functions.signature: _create_combo_load_case(load: OSLoad, currentLoadCaseId: int, comboCaseTitle: str, comboLoadCases: List[int], primary_case_ids: List[int], load_factors: List[float])
python_functions.purpose: Creates one STAAD combination and adds each nonzero primary-load factor. It advances the combination ID used by the caller.

python_functions.name: _verify_open_model
python_functions.purpose: Waits until STAAD reports the requested path and zero geometry counts. It proves the cleanup staging/original model actually opened before proceeding.

python_functions.name: prepare_saved_analysis
python_functions.purpose: Saves the generated STD, backs it up if correction is needed, inserts PerformAnalysis(0), saves again and checks serialized command order. It refuses to solve if the command is still absent.

python_functions.name: clean_staad
python_functions.purpose: Saves and backs up the current analytical STD, switches through an empty staging model, replaces/reopens the original path and verifies its saved tokens. It rejects physical models and active analysis; cleanup is not a rollback transaction.

python_functions.name: prepare_analysis_input
python_functions.purpose: Purely examines serialized command order and returns an idempotently prepared string with PERFORM ANALYSIS before DEFINE ENVELOPE. Ambiguous ordering or missing envelopes raise a validation error.

python_functions.name: analysis_errors
python_functions.purpose: Extracts solver ERROR lines and wrapped explanations from an ANL report so the user sees the root solver error instead of only missing downstream outputs.

python_functions.name: _get_connected_model
python_functions.purpose: Connects to Tekla's running model and verifies connectivity. The model must already be open and saved for the live workflow.

python_functions.name: _copy_missing_connection_attributes
python_functions.purpose: Copies missing reference attribute assets into the active model's attributes folder. Existing destination files are left untouched; this is not a silent overwrite of model-specific settings.

python_functions.name: _copy_missing_tekla_package_dbs
python_functions.purpose: Copies missing packaged Tekla database assets needed by the standard model. Existing files are preserved.

python_functions.name: delete_all_grids
python_functions.purpose: Legacy manual utility that explicitly deletes model grids. The automated cleanup path does not call it because it preserves grids.

python_functions.signature: create_grid(model: Model, X: str, Y: str, Z: str, labelX: str, labelY: str, labelZ: str, extensionLeftX: int, extensionLeftY: int, extensionLeftZ: int, extensionRightX: int, extensionRightY: int, extensionRightZ: int, originX: int, originY: int, originZ: int)
python_functions.purpose: Creates a Tekla grid with coordinate, label, extension and origin settings. This is an explicit model-changing helper.

python_functions.purpose: Updates existing grid coordinates/labels or delegates to the shared grid helper. A7 derives levels from the actual generated geometry instead of fixed sample heights.

python_functions.name: to_tekla_profile
python_functions.purpose: Normalizes profile strings to the installed Tekla naming convention before member creation and verification.

python_functions.name: _create_beam
python_functions.purpose: Creates one member in the relevant live application. In STAAD it resolves shared nodes and creates the analytical beam; in Tekla it sets physical endpoints, profile, material, class and positioning before insertion.

python_functions.name: _get_profile_parameter

python_functions.name: get_profile_height

python_functions.name: get_profile_width
python_functions.purpose: Returns the profile width from the installed Tekla catalogue; A7 validates that it is finite and positive.

python_functions.name: get_profile_web_thickness
python_functions.purpose: Reads the profile web/wall thickness used by the reference connection-geometry calculations.

python_functions.name: _index_to_letters
python_functions.purpose: Converts a positive grid index to spreadsheet-style labels, including rollover beyond Z.

python_functions.name: generate_y_axis_labels
python_functions.purpose: Creates the transverse grid-label sequence for the configured number of bays.

python_functions.name: get_bolt_parameters
python_functions.purpose: Returns the existing bolt-hole tolerance, hole diameter and edge-distance rule for the selected diameter. It supports reference detailing geometry; it does not replace IDEA bolt checks.

python_functions.name: clean_tekla
python_functions.purpose: Enumerates the active model, preserves grids/grid surfaces and DefaultGroup, removes components before remaining parts, verifies cleanup and saves. Optional callbacks report long scans/deletions; failures propagate.

python_functions.name: clean_tekla.snapshot
python_functions.purpose: Nested Tekla cleanup helper that snapshots deletable objects and preserved grid/default-group IDs, sorting components ahead of their generated parts.

python_functions.name: memberData2type
python_functions.purpose: Classifies a member-data record for load/design/grouping logic.

python_functions.name: memberName2type
python_functions.purpose: Classifies generated member names, including split beam and brace names, into consistent member categories.

python_functions.name: _get_top_node_coordinates
python_functions.purpose: Selects the coordinate records associated with the model's top-node IDs.

python_functions.name: _get_boundary_nodes
python_functions.signature: _get_boundary_nodes(node_cache: Dict[tuple, int], top_nodes: List[int], boundary_count: int)
python_functions.purpose: Classifies top nodes by boundary count for corner/edge/inner load distribution.

python_functions.name: _get_corner_nodes

python_functions.name: _get_edge_nodes
python_functions.purpose: Returns noncorner top nodes on the plan perimeter for load distribution.

python_functions.name: _get_inner_nodes

python_functions.name: _get_edge_members
python_functions.signature: _get_edge_members(members: List[Dict[str, Any]], node_cache: Dict[tuple, int], top_nodes: List[int])

python_functions.signature: _apply_radiator_wind_nodal_loads(load: OSLoad, node_cache: Dict[tuple, int], top_nodes: List[int], wind_case_title: str, load_configuration: Dict[str, Any], grid_spec: Dict[str, Any])

python_functions.purpose: Finds component extremes across load cases and joints while retaining governing case, node, member and end. Current selection includes columns and all six force/moment components.

python_functions.signature: build_joint_group_load_effects(joint_group: Dict[str, Any], forces_by_load_case: Dict[Any, dict[int, list[list[float]]]], load_cases: List[Any], load_case_titles: Dict[Any, str])

python_functions.signature: compute_summary_results(forces, forces_summary, support_reactions, support_reactions_summary, beam_node_map, node_displacements, node_displacements_summary, member_displacements, member_displacements_summary, lc, lc_title, joint_member_ends, summary_results)
python_functions.purpose: Applies the extrema helpers to one load case and updates the combined summary dictionary.

python_functions.name: send_to_staad

Live errors are not replaced by simulation.

python_functions.name: main
python_functions.purpose: Standalone adapter diagnostic entry point. It is separate from the managed A1-A8 server route and should not be confused with the normal workflow launcher.

python_functions.name: create_app
python_functions.purpose: Constructs the FastAPI application, request schemas, static UI, manual integration endpoints and agentic router. It defines the HTTP boundary; it does not itself perform a structural calculation.

python_functions.name: create_app.reserve_desktop_tools
python_functions.purpose: Rejects manual model-changing requests with HTTP 409 while this server's agentic controller owns the desktop tools. This protects against conflicting actions through this API, not against another unrelated application or server.

python_functions.name: create_app.radiator_support_ui
python_functions.purpose: Serves the radiator support HTML page. Rendering or refreshing this page is not an instruction to start a calculation.

python_functions.name: create_app.favicon
python_functions.purpose: Returns the application's icon asset to the browser.

python_functions.name: create_app.generate_radiator_support
python_functions.purpose: Validates the manual generation request and returns generated geometry and its summary. This keeps the senior application's manual generation route available.

python_functions.name: create_app.to_tekla
python_functions.purpose: Converts the manual Tekla request into the integration payload and calls the modeler. Actual adapter exceptions become HTTP errors rather than fabricated success.

python_functions.name: create_app.to_staad
python_functions.purpose: Converts the manual STAAD request into the analytical payload and awaits the live STAAD integration. It returns the actual analysis/result dictionary.

python_functions.name: create_app.to_ideastatica
python_functions.purpose: Passes a manual connection request to the IDEA adapter, excluding absent optional fields. It preserves the manual integration route alongside automation.

python_functions.name: start_api_server
python_functions.purpose: Builds the API application and starts Uvicorn using configured host and port. Development defaults bind to loopback.

python_functions.name: main
python_functions.purpose: Parses the server port, loads environment configuration and starts the local API. It is the application entry point used by start_server.bat.
